label: Aristotelian modality at every world: a non-actual accessible possibility is grounded in a power
paraphrase: OPEN (Aristotelian modality, stated once; analyst formulation of A. Pruss's principle, navigation only, attribution deferred): at every world u and for every proposition p, if p holds at some world accessible from u and fails at u, then some being existing at u has, at u, a power whose exercise would initiate a causal chain issuing in p (PowerFor u y p, the primitive of ModalGrounding). The single-proposition bare premises 95bf8780 (P1-prime, at w, for the joint absence of the concreta contingent at w), 607e94cf (at each world accessible from w that lacks them, for w obtaining) and 94393b5b (at w, for there being no contingent concretum) are instances of it. It says nothing about which being holds the power, whether the holder is concrete, necessary or unique, or whether the power is ever exercised; it is not PGP (powers over the existence of individuals).
